text:
Marina: quick follow-up from the RFC: should the canary fallback decision include per-tenant confidence scores + backpressure, or keep it in a simple global budget?
Devon: +1 to per-tenant. saw early customer case where one noisy tenant drowned the canary.
Alex: per-tenant helps fairness, but increases state & signaling. how do we keep routing fast?
Ira: SRE concern: more state => harder to reason under incident. can we bound it?
Marina: proposal idea: local router keeps a small sliding-window of tenant-level metrics (latency, error-rate, confidence) and consults a centralized policy service for thresholds. fallback decision is deterministic and cacheable for N seconds.
Sam: that hybrid seems fine. local caches avoid RPC on every request. need eviction & staleness rules.
Nina: from ML/quality POV, "confidence" is model-run output + histogram over recent tokens. it's noisy; we should smooth it and only use delta from baseline.
Devon: agree. we can represent tenant confidence as a percentile delta: p95_confidence_delta = current_p95_conf - baseline_p95_conf. fallback trigger when delta < -X and traffic > Y.
Alex: for interfaces: suggest a tiny policy blob per rollout: list of conditions, weights, and cooldowns. e.g.
Alex: ```json
{"policy_version":"v1","conditions":[{"metric":"p95_latency","op":">","value":300,"weight":0.5},{"metric":"p50_conf_delta","op":"<","value":-0.02,"weight":0.5}],"threshold":0.7,"cooldown_s":120}
```
Ira: cooldown + cooldown_jitter please. otherwise a noisy spike can flip flop.
Sam: also add "min-requests" so we don't evaluate tiny tenants.
Marina: good call. we should also specify ownership: control-plane owns policy blobs + rollout lifecycle, runtime owns local scoring and enforcement.
Devon: operationally, how do we surface why a request was routed to fallback? need trace headers.
Alex: add a simple reason header: X-Canary-Decision: fallback(reason=conf_delta,p95=420,threshold=0.7). keep it compact.
Nina: include anonymized metric snapshots for debug, but only for internal logs, not to customers.
Ira: during incident we need an expvar or /metrics scrape that shows per-tenant fallback counts and last-decision-reason.
Sam: implementation sketch: 1) control-plane publishes policy blob to konsul-like store 2) runtime subscribes and caches 3) runtime maintains per-tenant rolling windows 4) evaluate weighted score, apply cooldowns 5) emit header + metric.
Marina: API surface question: do we let SDKs opt into client-side prefiltering (i.e., SDK decides to route to stable model without roundtrip) vs forcing server-side only?
Devon: client-side is risky for security/observability. but SDK opt-in could reduce latency. we'd need signed policy tokens and a short TTL.
Alex: signed tokens feel like extra product complexity. maybe start server-side only, leave client-side as later perf optimization.
Ira: agreed. ship server-side first. instrument heavily.
Nina: for long-term refactor, we should design scoring as a composable pipeline: transforms -> aggregators -> evaluator. makes it easy to swap model-derived signals.
Marina: nice. that lets eng-ml plug different confidence transforms w/o changing routing.
Devon: any objections to the rollout steps? 1) proto policy schema, 2) local caching + eval, 3) rollout on a small subset of tenants, 4) observe for 2 weeks, 5) widen.
Ira: add a kill-switch and quick global disable route.
Sam: add telemetry dashboards: per-tenant fallback rate, latency delta, and revert events.
Marina: I'll draft the follow-up RFC with schema + migration plan. assign reviewers: @Devon, @Ira, @Nina, @Alex.
deploy-bot: noted: RFC draft created -> link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/pt-fallback-2026-draft :memo: (auto)
Devon: thanks — I can prototype the local cache + evaluator next sprint.
Alex: I'll prepare dashboard panels and alert rules.
Ira: I'll add runbook entries for fallback-on and fallback-off scenarios.
Sam: ping me when you have the policy schema, I'll wire the subscription path.
Marina: great, thanks all. closing this thread — please add comments on the draft RFC.
